page: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine configured with 32 dedicated physical cores running on 3.4 GHz ARM Neoverse-N2 silicon. Featuring a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the instance provides 64 GB of system RAM alongside an integrated 1890 GB NVMe SSD for fast scratch and caching workloads. The underlying architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache and 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, backed by 128 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware acceleration for AES cryptographic operations.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent multi-threaded compute and throughput capabilities. In multi-core assessments, the instance achieves top 25% performance in stress-ng (66,296.43) and Geekbench multi-core (19,774.0), complemented by strong execution in Clang software compilation. Memory subsystem performance is a notable strength, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 450.77 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 169.21 GB/sec, placing the memory subsystem in the top 10% of tested profiles. PassMark database operations also register in the top tier at 37,222.49.

The 2 GB of RAM per vCPU allocation represents a constraint for memory-heavy enterprise databases or large language model inference. For example, prompt processing with 70B parameter models falls into the bottom 10% (4.66 tokens/sec). However, the direct pairing of 32 physical cores with high memory bandwidth and fast local NVMe storage yields efficient compute density without the overhead of unneeded memory capacity.

The instance is suited for multi-threaded build systems, CI/CD compilation pipelines, high-throughput web serving, Redis caching, and transactional database tasks where working datasets comfortably fit within 64 GB of memory.
description: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v6 is an ARM-based compute instance powered by a 32-core ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 64 GB of memory, resulting in a 2 GB per core ratio, alongside a bundled 1890 GB NVMe SSD for high-speed local storage. Benchmark results show strong multi-core scaling, reaching top 25% percentiles in stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core workloads, as well as top-tier memory bandwidth exceeding 450 GB/sec for uncached reads. While the reduced memory-to-core ratio limits execution of massive in-memory models or large LLM prompt processing, the combination of dedicated execution threads, high memory throughput, and direct NVMe storage provides strong resource density. Azure D32plds_v6 functions effectively for continuous integration pipelines, Clang software compilation, Redis caching instances, and relational database servers with datasets optimized for local NVMe caching.
